lesson.scenario: Two workers decrement one versioned balance using a hardware-style atomic compare-and-swap loop.
entities: Attempts to subtract ten using an expected snapshot
Stores balance and version as one comparable value
Atomically compares expected word and installs replacement
connections: single atomic compare and conditional write

steps.title: A loads version 12
steps.narration: A reads the indivisible word balance 100, version 12 and computes replacement 90,13.
steps.outcome: A’s calculation is tied to the exact observed version.
steps.invariant: The expected value must include every field whose change invalidates the update.

steps.title: B loads the same version
steps.narration: Before A swaps, B reads version 12 and computes replacement 80,13.
steps.outcome: Both workers optimistically prepare from one snapshot.
steps.invariant: A load does not reserve the register or exclude competing writers.

steps.title: B wins the atomic swap
steps.narration: B’s expected word equals the current word, so CAS installs balance 80 at version 13.
steps.invariant: Comparison and replacement occur as one indivisible operation.

steps.title: A stale swap fails
steps.narration: A compares expected version 12 against current version 13; CAS returns failure and writes nothing.
steps.outcome: The lost-update race is detected instead of overwriting B.
steps.invariant: A failed CAS leaves the shared word bit-for-bit unchanged.

steps.title: A reloads and retries
steps.narration: A reads version 13, recomputes from balance 80, and successfully installs balance 70 at version 14.

audit.entries: v12→v13 by B; v13→v14 by A

steps.outcome: Both decrements are serialized as 100 to 80 to 70.
steps.invariant: Retry logic must recompute from the newly loaded value, not reuse a stale replacement.

production.scenario: A feature-flag control plane protects one checkout ramp setting in etcd so the release UI and the canary automation cannot silently overwrite each other during a Black Friday rollout.
components: Reads the current ramp revision before an operator changes checkout exposure
Owns checkout flag mutations and validation
Checks the expected etcd revision before a write is accepted
Authoritative ramp state and revision for the checkout flag
Carries the accepted flag snapshot to API gateways after the write commits
Shows operators when their write lost a race to automation
flows: The operator opens the checkout flag and loads revision 173 before touching the slider.
set ramp to 10 percent with expected revision 173
The UI submits both the new value and the exact revision it read so the server can reject stale intent.
compare expected revision against live revision
The flag API delegates the conditional write to the CAS guard instead of trusting the UI snapshot.
swap ramp to 10 percent and bump revision to 174
Only when the live row still matches revision 173 does etcd atomically replace the value and advance the revision.
Every gateway receives the same accepted config version and starts routing the 10 percent canary immediately.
If automation already moved the ramp to revision 174, the monitor surfaces the CAS failure so the operator reloads instead of clobbering the live state.
